cpmplus.art.err.noTexture: Open or select a texture first.
cpmplus.art.hint: CPM+: the art tools and the 44 brushes are in the "CPM+ Paint" panel, under the colour picker. Every button has its name written and the options show in the panel itself. Right-clicking a texture also has Model shading, Noise and Swap colour.
cpmplus.art.showAgain.desc: Opens the CPM+ art panel (if you closed or hid it) and puts the art buttons back in the Colour and Textures panels.
cpmplus.art.shade.desc: Lightens or darkens what is already painted without choosing a tone: light goes toward yellow and shade toward blue, like artists do. Choose Darken or Lighten in the panel; the right click does the opposite.
cpmplus.art.shade.mode.desc: How the brush picks the new tone. Warm/cool: lightens toward yellow and darkens toward blue, no palette needed. Ramp step: moves one tone along the ramp (only tones in the texture or your ramps). Hue/sat/light: adds the values you choose.
cpmplus.art.shade.dir.desc: What the left click does. The right click (Paint with secondary colour keybind) does the opposite.
cpmplus.art.shade.source.desc: Where the steps come from: the tones already in the texture (grouped by colour) or only your saved ramps.
cpmplus.art.shade.strength.desc: How much each pass lightens or darkens (15 = subtle, 40 = strong).
cpmplus.art.shade.hslH.desc: Degrees added to the hue (right click subtracts).
cpmplus.art.shade.hslS.desc: Points added to the saturation (right click subtracts).
cpmplus.art.shade.hslL.desc: Points added to the lightness (right click subtracts).
cpmplus.art.shade.once.desc: On: going over the same pixel again in the same stroke does not darken it more. Off: it builds up.
cpmplus.art.ramp.menu.desc: Creates the shadow and light tones of a colour (with the hue shift artists use), adds them to the palette and keeps them in My ramps.
cpmplus.art.ramp.title: Make colour ramp
cpmplus.art.ramp.intro: A ramp is the row of tones of a colour from darkest to lightest. Shadows lean to blue/purple and lights to yellow, like professional pixel art. Click a tone to use it as colour 1 (right click or Shift: colour 2).
cpmplus.art.ramp.hue.desc: How much the shadows turn blue and the lights yellow. 0 = only lighter/darker.
cpmplus.art.ramp.contrast.desc: Distance between the darkest and the lightest tone.
cpmplus.art.ramp.clickHint: Click: colour 1. Right click or Shift+click: colour 2.
cpmplus.art.ramp.mineEmpty: None yet. Save a ramp: the Shade brush (Ramp step mode) and the Pixel art gradient use them.
cpmplus.art.ramp.saved: Saved in My ramps (and set as the active ramp).
cpmplus.art.ramp.foundNone: No ramp with 2 or more tones in the texture.
cpmplus.art.ramp.paletteLocked: The palette is locked (padlock in the Color panel).
cpmplus.art.smudge.desc: Blends the tones already in the texture: drag over the border between two colours and the in-between tones appear, no colour to pick. It never paints where the texture is transparent or pulls colour from another face.
cpmplus.art.smudge.strength.desc: How much each pixel blends (100 = half of each colour at the border). With the pixel types, it is the chance of each pixel being swapped.
cpmplus.art.smudge.snap.desc: On: the result becomes the closest colour the texture already has (keeps the palette clean).
cpmplus.art.dither.desc: Paints a dot pattern (dithering) locked to the texture pixels: a transition between two colours without in-between tones, like pixel art. Right click paints the remaining cells with colour 2.
cpmplus.art.dither.pattern.desc: Shape of the dots. Bayer spreads them evenly (2×2 = checker at 50%); lines and diagonals suit cloth and shine; random dots suit sand and texture.
cpmplus.art.dither.density.desc: How many pixels of the pattern get the colour (50 = half).
cpmplus.art.dither.holes.desc: What happens to the pixels outside the pattern.
cpmplus.art.dither.shift.desc: Pushes the pattern a few pixels, to line the dots up between neighbouring faces of the model.
cpmplus.art.grad.menu.desc: Selects the Gradient already in the pixel art style (colour steps, dither between neighbouring tones, ramps). Blockbench's own Gradient button still makes the normal gradient.
cpmplus.art.grad.colors.desc: Where the tones come from. Right click reverses the direction.
cpmplus.art.grad.steps.desc: How many tones the gradient has (2 to 16).
cpmplus.art.grad.dither.desc: Mixes two neighbouring tones with dots instead of a straight line between them.
cpmplus.art.grad.shape.desc: Linear goes from where you start dragging to where you let go. Radial spreads in circles from the start point.
cpmplus.art.grad.noRamp: No active ramp: using colour 1 → colour 2. Make one in Make colour ramp.
cpmplus.art.noise.desc: Brings a flat area to life by varying the pixels one by one (controlled noise): a bit lighter or darker with warm light and cool shadow, one step of the texture tones, a touch of hue, or mixing colour 1 and colour 2. Each stroke changes a pixel once.
cpmplus.art.noise.mode.desc: How each pixel varies. Light/dark: warm light and cool shadow. Steps: one tone up or down, only tones that exist. Hue: the colour shifts a little. Colour 1 + 2: paints colour 1 or colour 2 at random.
cpmplus.art.noise.amount.desc: How much each pixel may change.
cpmplus.art.tnoise.menu.desc: Adds variation (noise) to the whole texture, the selection or only the selected parts, with a live preview.
cpmplus.art.tnoise.title: Texture noise
cpmplus.art.tnoise.intro: Varies the pixels so the area does not look flat. The preview shows on the model while you adjust; nothing really changes until Confirm (one Ctrl+Z undoes it). Same seed = same result.
cpmplus.art.swap.menu.desc: Swaps a whole family of tones (all the reds of the clothes, for example) for another colour, keeping the shading. Live preview, one Ctrl+Z undoes it.
cpmplus.art.swap.title: Swap colours (family)
cpmplus.art.swap.intro: The texture colours are grouped in families (same colour, dark to light). Click a family and change hue, saturation or brightness: all its tones change together and the shading stays the same. The preview shows on the model; nothing really changes until Confirm.
cpmplus.art.swap.none: Pick a colour family in the list.
cpmplus.art.swap.empty: The texture has no painted pixels.
cpmplus.art.as.menu.desc: Paints light and shadow on the texture understanding the model: light per face, top-to-bottom gradient, shadow where parts touch (neck, armpit, under the hair) and edges. Live preview, one Ctrl+Z undoes it.
cpmplus.art.as.title: Auto shading
cpmplus.art.as.intro: A first pass of light and shadow, worked out from the shape of the model (rest pose, no animation). It lightens and darkens what is already painted, in warm-light / cool-shadow tones or in the tones the texture already has. Then just touch it up by hand. The preview shows on the model; nothing really changes until Confirm.
cpmplus.art.as.noCubes: No textured cube face to shade.
cpmplus.art.as.light.top_left: Top and the character's left side
cpmplus.art.as.face.desc: Faces turned to the light get lighter and the opposite ones darker (in tone steps).
cpmplus.art.as.vertical.desc: The whole model gets lighter at the top and darker at the bottom, across all parts.
cpmplus.art.as.ao.desc: Darkens where a part touches or comes close to another (neck, armpit, under the hair, between fingers).
cpmplus.art.as.range.desc: Up to which distance (in model pixels) another part casts shadow.
cpmplus.art.as.edge.desc: How many tone steps the edge gets.
cpmplus.art.as.tone.ramp: Only tones the texture already has
cpmplus.art.as.step.desc: How much each step lightens or darkens in the warm light / cool shadow mode.
cpmplus.art.br.desc: Paints with the brush picked in the CPM+ Paint panel (44 community brushes remade for 64×64 skins).
cpmplus.art.br.menu.desc: Opens the CPM+ Paint panel at the brushes, with a preview of each one.
cpmplus.art.br.preset.desc: Which library brush the Brushes tool paints with.
cpmplus.art.br.scatter.desc: How far the stamps, strands and dots spread around the stroke (100% = the brush's own amount, 0% = on the line).
cpmplus.art.br.vary.desc: How much the size and tone of each stamp, strand or dot vary (0% = all the same, 200% = very varied).
cpmplus.art.br.p.lapis.desc: Dark graphite that thins out at the start and end of the stroke; the paper grain shows at the edge and where the stroke is light. On 64×64 skins: grain dots in tones of colour 1.
cpmplus.art.br.p.lineart.desc: Lineart pen that tapers at the start and the end of the stroke. At size 1 it draws pixel-perfect lines (no double steps on curves).
cpmplus.art.br.p.contorno.desc: Paints colour 1 with a 1-pixel outline around it in a darker tone of the same colour.
cpmplus.art.br.p.contorno2.desc: Paints colour 1 with a 1-pixel outline in colour 2.
cpmplus.art.br.p.render.desc: Soft brush for painting and rendering: covers in the middle, has a soft edge and mixes a little with the colour underneath, carrying it along the stroke. Thins out at the ends. On 64×64 skins it only blends where there is colour.
cpmplus.art.br.p.renderpx.desc: A very light airbrush that builds up and pulls in the colour underneath: go over the border between two colours to blend them. On 64×64 skins it is made of dithering (no new colour).
cpmplus.art.br.p.aquarela.desc: Transparent paint that mixes a little with the colour underneath and is stronger at the edge of the stroke.
cpmplus.art.br.p.oleo.desc: Flat brush with thick paint: covers, leaves bristle marks and drags a little of the colour underneath.
cpmplus.art.br.p.arcoiris.desc: The colour cycles through the rainbow along the stroke (starting at colour 1).
cpmplus.art.br.p.pixel.desc: Shortcut: selects Blockbench's Brush at 1 pixel, no softness, pixel-perfect on.
cpmplus.art.br.p.cabelo.desc: Several 1-pixel strands that follow the stroke, in lighter and darker tones of colour 1. Starts thin and opens up.
cpmplus.art.br.p.cachos.desc: Little curls turned toward the stroke direction, for curly and coily hair.
cpmplus.art.br.p.brilhocabelo.desc: Shine strands: they lighten the colour already painted (the colour is not replaced). Go over the hair where the light hits.
cpmplus.art.br.p.pelo.desc: A lock of fur with fine hairs that thins out at the start and end, for fur, beards and fluffy clothes. On 64×64 skins: short tufts.
cpmplus.art.br.p.penas.desc: Feathers with a light shaft and fine barbs, one after the other along the stroke, for wings. On 64×64 skins: V marks.
cpmplus.art.br.p.escamas.desc: Scales fixed to the texture with a highlight on top and shade below (dragons, mermaids, snakes). The brush size sets the scale size.
cpmplus.art.br.p.grama.desc: Grass blades growing upward in tones of colour 1.
cpmplus.art.br.p.folhas.desc: Scattered, turned leaves with a dark vein.
cpmplus.art.br.p.flores.desc: Scattered little flowers: petals in colour 1, centre in colour 2.
cpmplus.art.br.p.nuvens.desc: Painted clouds with a bumpy edge, a light top and a darker base. Paint with 2 or 3 tones for volume.
cpmplus.art.br.p.fogo.desc: A ribbon of fire: an almost white core, flames licking out to the sides and a glow around; thins out at the ends. Use orange as colour 1. On 64×64 skins: stamped flames.
cpmplus.art.br.p.respingos.desc: Scattered drops of different sizes: blood, mud, paint.
cpmplus.art.br.p.bolhas.desc: Round bubbles with a shine dot.
cpmplus.art.br.p.glitter.desc: Scattered dots in several tones of colour 1, with white sparks.
cpmplus.art.br.p.brilhos.desc: Cross-shaped sparkles that lighten the colour underneath (eyes, metal, jewels, magic).
cpmplus.art.br.p.estrelas.desc: Scattered little stars of different sizes.
cpmplus.art.br.p.neon.desc: Almost white core with a colour 1 halo around it. With a small brush the halo is dithered.
cpmplus.art.br.p.blush.desc: Translucent cheek blush (dithered at small sizes) with tiny white sparkles.
cpmplus.art.br.p.olhos.desc: Iris stamp: dark pupil, white shine dot and eyelid shade on top. Click once on each eye.
cpmplus.art.br.p.renda.desc: Scalloped lace trim, for hems and dresses.
cpmplus.art.br.p.perolas.desc: A row of shiny pearls, for necklaces and trims.
cpmplus.art.br.p.corrente.desc: Alternating chain links (one round, one side-on).
cpmplus.art.br.p.cicatriz.desc: A dark cut with cross stitches in colour 2.
cpmplus.art.br.p.xadrez.desc: Checker in colour 1 and colour 2, fixed to the texture (going over it again stays aligned). The brush size sets the square size.
cpmplus.art.br.p.listras.desc: Diagonal stripes in colour 1 and colour 2, fixed to the texture.
cpmplus.art.br.p.bolinhas.desc: Colour 1 dots over what is already painted, fixed to the texture.
cpmplus.art.br.p.escoces.desc: Tartan: colour 1 background, colour 2 bands and darker crossings.
cpmplus.art.br.p.jeans.desc: Diagonal denim weave in tones of colour 1.
cpmplus.art.br.p.trico.desc: V-shaped knit stitches, for sweaters and beanies.
cpmplus.art.br.p.papel.desc: Paper texture: lightens and darkens what is already painted a little, in patches.
cpmplus.art.br.p.grao.desc: Fine grain: some pixels of what is already painted get one tone lighter or darker.
cpmplus.art.br.p.reticula.desc: Halftone dots on a grid (manga and comics style) in colour 1.
cpmplus.art.panel.hint: Pick a tool or a brush and paint.
cpmplus.art.panel.none: Pick a brush or a tool above: its options show up here.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.shade: Go over what is already painted.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.smudge: Drag over the border between two colours: the in-between tones appear.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.smudgepx: Drag over the border between two colours: it becomes a checker of both, no new colour.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.dither: Paints dots lined up with the pixels in colour 1.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.noise: Go over a flat area: each pixel changes a little.
cpmplus.art.panel.tip.grad: Drag from where the gradient starts to where it ends (colour 1 to colour 2).
cpmplus.art.panel.toast: CPM+: the art tools and the brushes now live in the "CPM+ Paint" panel, under the colour picker. Every button has its name written and the options show in the panel itself.
cpmplus.art.smudge.kind.desc: Blend makes the in-between tones (default). Drag the colour pulls the colour along the stroke, like a finger. Drag pixels and Jumble pixels only move whole pixels, no new colour.
cpmplus.art.smudgepx.desc: Blends two pixel-art colours without making a new one: drag over the border and the pixels on both sides become a checker of the two colours. Going over it again widens the blend.
cpmplus.art.smudgepx.menu.desc: Selects the Pixel smudge tool (Paint mode).
cpmplus.art.br.style.desc: HD: smooth brushes with drawn tips, clean edges and texture, for big textures (128 px or more). Pixel art: stamps made pixel by pixel, no new colour, for 64×64 skins. Automatic picks by the texture size.
cpmplus.art.br.p.folhagem.desc: Foliage tufts with a jagged edge, in one flat colour: click to stamp a tuft or drag for a band. For volume, paint the dark tone first and a lighter one on top (grass, bushes, tree crowns).
